title: Draymond Green Fires Back At Alperen Sengun After Bold Accusation Of Warriors "Crying" For Fouls While Playing Dirty - NewsBreak
text: The Golden State Warriors have drawn attention this season for making no roster moves. Although they pursued several free agents, including Al Horford, none were signed. Amid this, Houston Rockets star Alperen Sengun criticized the Warriors for their performance last season. Sengun claimed the Warriors often complained to referees about fouls while playing with excessive physicality . In fact, last season, NBA fans witnessed some heated on-court clashes between Sengun and Warriors veteran Draymond Green . Following Sengun’s most recent comments, Green reignited the rivalry and clapped back at him. “ That’s a tough thing to say after you lose… You have to win to [say] stuff like that ,” Green wrote. Green was clearly pointing to the Rockets-Warriors first-round matchup. Despite Sengun’s standout play, Houston rallied from a 3-1 deficit to force a Game 7. Ultimately, however, the Warriors had the last laugh by eliminating Sengun and the Rockets from the playoffs. Still, Green’s squad failed to progress beyond the following round. This offseason, Alperen Sengun’s training is centered on long-range shooting. In an interview with MeridianSport, Sengun’s personal trainer, Djordje Sijan, opened up about the Rockets center’s work behind the scenes. “ This year we focused mostly on 3-point shooting. That shot was forbidden for him before. There’s big pressure on him to shoot more. The NBA is modern basketball, they want him to be a five or four who can stretch. We worked from day one to the last, perfecting his shooting mechanics. Now he needs mental stability and confidence. Shot selection is key ,” Sijan said. Sengun is coming off a season where he averaged 19.1 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 4.9 assists per game. The numbers already place him among the most well-rounded big men in the league. Yet in today’s NBA, the ability to step out beyond the arc could unlock a new level for his career. The post originally published on .
